sysSecurity.allowedDomainsTooltip:
1. Only applies to public link access under Whitelist Mode
2. One host per line, in the form host:port (e.g. 192.168.1.3:5505, img.example.com:8443). Same host on a different port counts as a different source
3. Matching is by the source's host + port: both must match. Paths and query strings are ignored
4. Example: allowing 192.168.1.3:5505 lets any page under http://192.168.1.3:5505/ (including /?id=29, /post/29.html) through, but a request from 192.168.1.3:55105 is still blocked (different port)
5. Pasting a full URL is fine (only the host + port is kept). Empty = no restriction

The response header returns this site's signed link. If your client builds URLs itself, set the custom domain to the access domain above.
sysSecurity.webUsageTip: Put the token in a custom Body field to upload. Optional username / userstore: when username is passed and userstore is not false, the account's storage/backup channels from User Management are used and the file belongs to that account; otherwise the channel is taken from this token's storage/backup channels → the global default in Channel Settings. Compression is controlled by the compress field: send true / 1 to compress (GIF is skipped), or omit it to upload as-is. The returned url is the link issued by this site.

sysSecurity.webJsonPathTip: Set the JSON path to "url" to return the full data packet, or to "data.url" to return only the file link value.

sysSecurity.enforceLimitsTooltip: On (default): files sent with this token are restricted by the allowed formats and per-file size cap in "Upload settings". Off: both restrictions are skipped. Applies to both Web and S3 tokens.
sysSecurity.mailConfigTooltip:

· Redirect: 302 to the given URL

sysOthers.webdavTooltip:
When enabled, this system can be mounted as a network drive (Finder / Explorer / RaiDrive).
Mount URL: https://your-domain/dav/
Account: normal user accounts only (admin accounts cannot use WebDAV)
Password: the access key of a channel created under User Management → WebDAV management (16 random characters, regenerable; the old key stops working immediately)
Turning this off disables WebDAV globally: mounted clients can no longer read or write.
sysOthers.webdavChannelHint: The upload channel is no longer configured here: it follows the account's main/backup channel in User Management, and falls back to the global channels in Channel Settings.
sysOthers.webdavAccountNote: How it works: first enable "Enable WebDAV" for a normal user in User Management → Edit account → Admin actions and set the channel limit (default 2), then create channels (name / storage path / access key / note) in that user WebDAV management. Files are stored as-is following the standard WebDAV protocol in the server webdav directory (/app/backend/webdav/{username}/{storage path}) — no renaming, compression, transcoding or WebP conversion, and no file type or size limits. Files transferred over WebDAV never appear in Image Files or History and cannot be compressed, transcoded, converted to WebP or moved to remote storage from the file details page. Admin accounts cannot use WebDAV.
sysOthers.tagAddSettingsTooltip: Tags added automatically after a successful upload, according to the rules below. All three rule types can be combined and results are de-duplicated (20 chars per tag, 30 tags at most). Leave everything empty to keep only the tags the caller passes explicitly (e.g. "local upload" / "video snapshot").
sysOthers.tagRuleOffHint: Automatic tagging is off: the rules below are still saved, but no tags are added after upload until you turn the switch above on.
sysOthers.tagPlaceholdersTooltip:
Compose the tag names to add from placeholders. Separate with commas or newlines — each segment becomes one tag.
Supported: {mime} file type (image / video / audio), {ext} extension without the dot, {channelName} channel type short name, {uploadSource} upload source, {y} year (4 digits), {m} month (2 digits), {d} day (2 digits), {width} width, {height} height.
Placeholders with no value (e.g. {width} for a non-image) are skipped, so no empty or half-built tags are produced.
sysOthers.tagExtractTooltip:
Map "text found in the file name" to "tag to add", format: ["text":"tag"].
Example: ["maomi":"cat"] adds the tag "cat" when the file name contains maomi.
Multiple pairs are allowed: ["maomi":"cat","wedding":"wedding day"].
sysOthers.tagRegexTooltip:
Takes one segment of the file name between a start marker and a stop marker as a tag, dropping it when it exceeds the length limit.
Both fields take raw symbols, and every character is a separate marker (e.g. #{'@'}& means # or {'@'} or &); leave a field empty to use the default.
Example: start #{'@'}&, stop #{'@'}&!, at most 10 characters — #cat-photo!final.png yields the tag "cat-photo".
Consecutive start markers use the last one (##tag → "tag"); whitespace is always a stop marker; listing the start markers again as stop markers lets #food#scenery split at the second #.
sysOthers.tagStartCharsPlaceholder: e.g. # , {'@'} , & (an empty entry means start of name)
sysOthers.tagRuleHint: Enter raw symbols in both fields — every character is a separate marker (e.g. #{'@'}& gives three start markers). Leave a field empty to use the default; whitespace is always a stop marker. Content longer than the limit is dropped entirely (0 = no limit).
